brief: A record de-grossing stretch across US long/short hedge funds between July and October turned into an outright net leverage reduction this week: net leverage fell 5% on Thursday alone to 42%, the 5th largest single-day decline since 2010, leaving nets 8% lower week over week, the lowest level all year though still above April 2025's roughly 35% lows. Gross leverage ended at 202%, pushing toward 12-month troughs. Midterm elections cleared a political overhang but did not prompt re-risking; funds used Wednesday's relief rally to keep de-grossing both sides of the book into Thursday's broader long-side supply event. With L/S gross flow over recent months at -10.7% of global gross market value as of end-June, positioning imbalances across sectors, factors and themes are now moderate, so hedge funds no longer appear to be the driver of sharp reversals, though they remain sensitive enough to accelerate moves in either direction. AI-theme net exposure has fallen to about 32% of total US net exposure from a 47% June peak, leaving funds about 2% underweight those names. Despite the volatility, L/S PnL held up relatively well, and funds captured less than 30% of the S&P's Thursday losses.
